news.title: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
paras: Attitude adjustment Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors This was the first total mission failure in United Launch Alliance’s 20-year history. A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket lifts off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, at 12:40 pm local time Sunday.

Sunday’s failure is expected to ground the rocket for an indefinite period of time. Vulcan is no stranger to close calls, having overcome failures with its strap-on solid rocket boosters on two of its four previous flights. In each case, the rocket corrected for those problems and continued into orbit to deploy its payloads.

news.title: Skeleton found in Denmark came from man who witnessed the arrival of farming
paras: “What was it like to live through such a momentous transition, seeing the archipelago where your ancestors had fished being transformed by the arrival of a new group of people?” says Anders Fischer at the University of Gothenburg in Sweden. Rødhals Man lived some 6000 years ago, and was discovered on the small island of Sejerø in Denmark in the 1950s, buried in a shell midden – an ancient accumulation of discarded sea shells and other domestic refuse.

Previous investigations have indicated he was unusual. He lived some time between about 3800 and 3900 BC, near the start of the Neolithic period in the area, when diets changed to consist predominantly of terrestrial food produced by farmers.

sport.title: How Aryna Sabalenka’s record and prize money from the 2026 WTA season compares to 2025
paras: After losing the Australian Open final to Elena Rybakina , the former world number one bounced back emphatically, winning Indian Wells and the Miami Open. At the time, it seemed the Belarusian would go on to dominate proceedings on the WTA Tour throughout 2026.

Sabalenka went on to suffer a plethora of early exits at significant WTA Tour events: including a concerning defeat to Diana Shnaider at the French Open , and a worrisome performance against Jessica Pegula in Berlin. Sabalenka has done little to improve her situation since the summer , and has now fallen to world number three for the first time since August 12, 2024.

sport.title: Madison Keys gives her opinion on Mirra Andreeva’s behaviour vs Elina Svitolina in the final of the WTA Finals
paras: Mirra Andreeva has capped off a sensational WTA Finals debut by lifting the trophy in Indian Wells. Andreeva shared her delight at winning the WTA Finals title, which she did via a 7-5, 6-3 final victory over Elina Svitolina .

She had also beaten her WTA rival in the group stages, having also claimed wins over Aryna Sabalenka and Diana Shnaider. Following that, Andreeva overcame Jessica Pegula in the semifinals of the year-end tournament, shortly after the American had bad-mouthed her Russian counterpart. During a practice session in Indian Wells, when she was unaware that her comments were public, Pegula labelled Andreeva a “diva” and said she needed to be “put in her place”.

sport.title: Ben Shelton Sees Off Fils To Clinch First ATP Finals Win of Career
paras: Ben Shelton described his win over Arthur Fils as a ‘ pretty physical and tough contest ‘ after battling past the Frenchman in three sets. Shelton, who reached his maiden Grand Slam final at the US Open earlier this year, overcame Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-3 after two hours of play.

The American looked to be cruising towards a comfortable victory after winning his first seven service games without facing a break point. However, his momentum stalled in the second set as Fils reeled off three consecutive games to force a decider.

sport.title: Mirra Andreeva has message for Elina Svitolina in winner’s speech immediately after beating her at the WTA Fin
paras: Mirra Andreeva has sent a heartfelt message of commiserations to Elina Svitolina after beating her in the final of the WTA Finals. After one hour and 48 minutes in Indian Wells, Andreeva defeated Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to secure the title.

The Russian superstar has emerged victorious on her WTA Finals debut. But rather than focus on her own stunning success, Andreeva was quick to praise Svitolina after their exciting encounter. In a classy winner’s speech, the 19-year-old said to her opponent: “I just want to congratulate Elina and the team for an amazing week.

sport.title: Mirra Andreeva Sinks Svitolina To Become Youngest WTA Finals Champion Since Sharapova
paras: Mirra Andreeva capped off her dream run at the WTA Finals with a tightly contested two-set triumph over Elina Svitolina to win the title on her tournament debut. The 19-year-old battled to a 7-5, 6-3 win over 2018 champion Svitolina during what was a roller-coaster encounter in Indian Wells.

A total of nine breaks occurred during the 109-minute match, with six of those being in Andreeva’s favour. Overall, she converted six out of 16 break point opportunities. “Coming into this match, it was the second time in my life where I thought that I’m just gonna die on the court, she’s not getting the win,” Andreeva told Sky Sports.

sport.title: Mirra Andreeva issues strong message after winning the WTA Finals, ‘she is not getting the win’
paras: The Russian youngster maintained her flawless status at the end-of-year event, beating Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Sunday’s final. It was another superb performance by the young Russian, who has also defeated Aryna Sabalenka, Diana Shnaider and Jessica Pegula in the past week.

Andreeva was particularly effective off the return, winning 52 per cent of all points off Svitolina’s first serve, as reported by Sofascore . “It was the second time in my life where I just thought I am going to die on the court but she is not getting the win,” Andreeva told Sky Sports in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s blockbuster.
